The correct count is 72, so Solution 3 is right. The count works as follows. Every row and column must be a triple from {1,…,9} summing to 15, and there are exactly two ways to split the digits into three such triples: A = {159, 267, 348} and B = {168, 249, 357}. Rows and columns must use different partitions, since any triple of A meets another triple of A in one digit only if the partitions differ. With rows from A and columns from B (or the reverse), each cell is forced to be the intersection of its row triple and column triple. Ordering the rows and columns gives 3! × 3! = 36 grids for each choice, for 72 in total. Solution 1 (576) and Solution 2 (8) are wrong.
